name: Angostura Recreation Area (Cascade Campground)
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-22: Esri World_Imagery at 330 m half-width and 130 m half-width (0.29 m/px) over the west row, every Go Outdoors SD facID=3 loop 1 (Cascade) unit point plotted; all frames rendered; plus the engine's own site photos of 27E, 29E, 31E, 33E, 35E, 38E, 40E, 42E, 44E and 71E. The west row 26E-44E sits inside a continuous band of shore trees; today's imagery (a drawdown year) puts ~120-140 m of bare sand flat between that band and the water. The site photos (taken at a high pool) show the lake through and among the trees from 27E-44E; at 29E and 31E the water reaches the tree line ~30-40 m off, with trees standing in it. Open-Meteo puts 31E at 971 m, at the reservoir's top of conservation pool (3,187.2 ft = 971.5 m, Reclamation). Even at full pool the view is through a belt of trees, and the water is usually far below it, so not lakefront -> lakeview.
inclusion_evidence: Go Outdoors SD engine https://reservations.gooutdoorssouthdakota.com/FacilityDetails.aspx?facID=3 ('Angostura Recreation Area'), sitesHashMap read 2026-11-22, active units of loop 1 (Cascade): 63 web-bookable electric RV sites 26E-89E (no 57E), back-ins plus pull-thru 71E (140 ft), 'Amp Service: 20/30/50', MaxEquipLength 36-140 ft, UnitBasePrice $30; camping cabins C1, C2, C10, C15 ($60); V4/V5 'Campground Host' ($37). GFP campground map https://gfp.sd.gov/userdocs/angostura_campgrounds.pdf (ArcGIS Pro, 2023-05-23): the same numbering, V4/V5 host sites, two restroom/shower buildings, vault toilet, water; arrows 'To Beach & Cascade Campground' from Cheyenne and 'To Hat Creek & Horsehead Campground'. Overview map https://gfp.sd.gov/userdocs/angostura_overview.pdf: Cascade on its own loop road off the park road with a swim beach at its north end. Esri imagery 2026-11-22: gravel pads at the unit points on Cascade's own loops. Real drive-in RV campground; a 23-ft rig fits every RV site (shortest 36 ft). 2.33 km from Cheyenne and 2.15 km from Hat Creek RV-site centroid to centroid (nearest sites 17E-26E 2.05 km, 48E-90E 1.92 km). Not in the DB before (split from 5714 Angostura Recreation Area, 2026-11-22). Public (state): no price gate.
note: Angostura Recreation Area's Cascade campground, on its own loop road off the park road about 2 km south of the north entrance, with a swim beach at its north end. The west row (26E-44E) is in a belt of shore trees; when the reservoir is down a wide sand flat lies between the trees and the water. Cheyenne to the north, and Hat Creek with Horsehead to the south, are separate entries. --Claude

sites.note: Plus camping cabins C1, C2, C10 and C15. 71E is the one pull-thru; the longest back-in is 70 ft (60E).

season.note: October 1 to April 30 the showers, flush toilets and water may be off; vault toilets stay open.

fees.note: GFP publishes this park's own rate: electric $30 a night (the statewide $7 electrical fee is already in the figure); the park's $16 non-electric sites are tent-only, in the Cheyenne loop. Residents and non-residents pay the same to camp; the entrance licence and the $10 non-resident reservation fee are what differ.

name: Angostura Recreation Area (Hat Creek and Horsehead Campgrounds)
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-22: Esri World_Imagery at 650 m half-width over both, 130 m half-width (0.29 m/px) over Hat Creek and over Horsehead's west side, 150 m half-width over Horsehead's south side, every Go Outdoors SD facID=3 loop 4 (Hat Creek) and loop 5 (Horsehead) unit point plotted; all frames rendered; plus the engine's own site photos of 94E, 96E, 98E, 99E, 100E, 101E, 125E-128E, 137E, 139E, 142E, 144E, 146E. Today's imagery is a drawdown year: Hat Creek's 98E, 100E and 101E sit ~10-25 m from the grass/sand line and ~75-90 m over open sand from the water; Horsehead's 127E ~70 m and 142E ~75 m from the water through a belt of shore trees. The site photos (taken at a high pool) show water directly behind 96E, 98E, 100E and 101E across open grass, past shrubs at 94E, glimpses through trees at 128E, 142E and 144E, and none at 99E, 125E-127E, 137E, 139E, 146E. Open-Meteo puts the pin at 972 m against a top of conservation pool of 971.5 m (3,187.2 ft, Reclamation); the reservoir stood at 48% of capacity in July 2026 (Reclamation). Lakefront only at a pool the reservoir seldom holds, so held down per the drawdown rule -> lakeview.
inclusion_evidence: Go Outdoors SD engine https://reservations.gooutdoorssouthdakota.com/FacilityDetails.aspx?facID=3 ('Angostura Recreation Area'), sitesHashMap read 2026-11-22: loop 4 (Hat Creek) 23 web-bookable electric RV sites 90E-112E and loop 5 (Horsehead) 51, 113E-163E, every one 'Back-In Campsite', 'Amp Service: 20/30/50', MaxEquipLength 32-74 ft (144E's 75 looks like the engine default and was not used), UnitBasePrice $30; camping cabins C3, C4, C11, C12, C13 (Hat Creek) and C7, C8 (Horsehead); V6, V7, V8 'Campground Host' ($37). GFP campground map https://gfp.sd.gov/userdocs/angostura_campgrounds.pdf (ArcGIS Pro, 2023-05-23): the same numbering, host sites marked, a restroom/shower building in each, vault toilets, water, Hat Creek's arrow 'To South Entrance & Horsehead Campground'. Overview map https://gfp.sd.gov/userdocs/angostura_overview.pdf: both off the park road near the south entrance with day-use area #3 (ramp, fishing pier, fish cleaning, shelter) between them. Esri imagery 2026-11-22: gravel pads at the unit points, each campground on its own spur off the park road. Real drive-in RV campground; a 23-ft rig fits every RV site (shortest 32 ft, 112E). Hat Creek and Horsehead are only 720 m apart centroid to centroid (nearest sites 101E-127E 424 m) and share the south entrance, so they are one entry; 2.59 km from Cascade and 4.81 km from Cheyenne. Not in the DB before (split from 5714 Angostura Recreation Area, 2026-11-22). Public (state): no price gate.
note: Angostura Recreation Area's two south campgrounds, Hat Creek (90E-112E) and Horsehead (113E-163E), each on its own spur off the park road from the south entrance, with a day-use area between them (boat ramp, fishing pier, fish cleaning station, picnic shelter). Hat Creek's shore sites 94E-101E face the water across grass at a high pool; when the reservoir is down a wide sand flat lies between. Cheyenne and Cascade to the north are separate entries. --Claude
